title: Japan that children can experience for themselves
intro: Come and enjoy Japan Day with your children in a slightly different way. We are preparing creative activities, traditional Japanese games, sweet treats and a colouring competition with Japanese motifs.

activities.title: Colouring Japanese motifs
activities.short: Colour pictures inspired by Japan and take part in the competition.
activities.description: Children will receive prepared pictures with Japanese and anime themes that they can colour using their own imagination. Finished pictures can be entered in the competition for the best-coloured motif.

activities.title: Origami
activities.description: Children and parents can try origami, the traditional Japanese art of paper folding, and create their own simple paper model.

activities.title: Ayatori あやとり
activities.short: A traditional Japanese game played with a loop of string.
activities.description: Different patterns and figures are created with the fingers and a loop of string. Ayatori is a simple and entertaining game that develops fine motor skills, concentration and coordination.

activities.title: Shogi 将棋
activities.description: Children and adults can try shogi, a traditional Japanese strategy game similar to chess, and learn the basic rules.

activities.title: Japanese sweets
activities.description: Various Japanese and Asian sweets and small treats for children and adults will be available throughout the day.

competition.title: Colour Japan with your imagination!
competition.intro: We are preparing a colouring competition with Japanese motifs for children.

categories.title: Best-coloured picture
categories.intro: The competition is intended mainly for our youngest visitors.
categories.body: At the venue you will receive prepared pictures with Japanese and anime themes that you can colour using your own imagination.
categories.detail: Pick up your coloured pencils and get started!
categories.evaluation: especially the idea, use of colour, precision and overall impression.

prize.title: A prize awaits the winner.
prize.text: The most important thing is to use your imagination, have fun and enjoy Japan Day with us.

archive.title: Children's Art Competition 2026
archive.intro: The Japanese Tea and Culture Day also included a children's art competition. Thank you to all the children who took part and showed us how they see Japan through their pictures.

categories.title: Japanese motif colouring
categories.intro: The competition was intended especially for the youngest visitors.
categories.body: Pictures with Japanese and anime themes were available at the event for children to colour using their imagination.
categories.detail: Children could use coloured pencils and their imagination to create their pictures.
categories.evaluation: originality, use of colour, precision and overall impression.

prize.title: Announced prize
prize.text: The competition encouraged children's imagination and creativity. Results and winners' names are not listed here.

activity.title: Children's art competition
activity.short: Children shared how they see Japan through their pictures.
activity.description: Children created pictures with Japanese and anime motifs at Japanese Tea and Culture Day.

safety.title: Supervision of children
safety.text: Children’s activities are not a childcare service. Children remain under the supervision and responsibility of a parent or another accompanying adult at all times.

archiveIntro: The programme for children and families featured creative activities, traditional Japanese games, origami, ayatori and an art competition.
